Rashi on Nedarim 59b:1:1.hebrew: אתוספת קתני - דאסורין לאכלן בשמינית, דחייב לבערן, אבל העיקר שרי, דאמרינן: היתר שבהן להיכן הלך:
Rashi on Nedarim 59b:1:1.english: It is taught regarding the additional [growth] - That they are forbidden to eat in the eighth [year], for one is obligated to remove them, but the primary [onion] is permitted, for we say: "The permitted part in them, where did it go?"

Rashi on Nedarim 59b:1:2.english: That which grew during [a period of] liability - In the Sabbatical year, [it] is liable for removal.

Rashi on Nedarim 59b:1:3.hebrew: והגדיל בפטור - דזהו העיקר הגדל בששית, פטור. הכי נמי קאמר תנא קמא כו':
Rashi on Nedarim 59b:1:3.english: And that which grew during [a period of] exemption - For this is the primary [part] that grew in the sixth [year], [which is] exempt. So too does the first Tanna say, etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 59b:2:1.hebrew: תריץ: כולה מתניתין <abbr title="רבי">ר'</abbr> שמעון בן גמליאל קתני לה, והכי קתני: <abbr title="שרבן שמעון בן גמליאל">שרשב"ג</abbr> אומר "הגדל כו'". ולעולם <abbr title="אמרינן">אמרי'</abbr> היתר שבהם להיכן הלך? וקא מהדר גמרא: <abbr title="לעולם">לעול'</abbr>, <abbr title="ואפילו">ואפי'</abbr> לר"ש לא <abbr title="אמרינן">אמרי'</abbr> היתר שבהן להיכן הלך, ועד כאן לא אמר <abbr title="רבן שמעון בן גמליאל">רשב"ג</abbr> "הגדל בפטור פטור" — דאמרינן היתר שבהן להיכן הלך, דלא קא בטיל היתר — היכא דלא קא טרח, כגון התם, שירדו עליהן גשמים וצמחו מאיליהן. אבל היכא דקא טרח, כגון הכא דנטען, כדקתני "שתיקנה וזרעה", הואיל ועבד בה מעשה, גידולין של איסור מבטלין את ההיתר והוי הכל אסור; להכי מתעשר לפי כולה:
Rashi on Nedarim 59b:2:1.english: [The Gemara] resolves [it]: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel taught the entire Mishnah, and this is what it teaches: "For Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: That which grows, etc." And [yet] do we always say, "Where did the permitted [part] in them go?" And the Gemara responds: Actually, even according to R. Shimon [ben Gamliel], we do not [always] say, "Where did the permitted [part] in them go?" Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel only said "that which grows [from something] exempt is exempt" — where we say "where did the permitted [part] in them go?" so that the permitted [part] is not neutralized — [in a case] where he did not exert himself, such as there, where rain fell upon them and they sprouted on their own. However, where he exerted himself, such as here where he planted them — as [the Mishnah] teaches, "that he prepared [the bed] and sowed it" — since he performed an action on it, the forbidden growths neutralize the permitted [part] and the whole becomes forbidden; therefore, it is tithed according to its entirety.

Rashi on Nedarim 59b:3:1.english: He tithes for it according to calculation - Even though he exerts himself with respect to the rest of the growths.

Rashi on Nedarim 59b:3:2.hebrew: היתירא זרעי אינשי - דבר שהוא מתוקן, רגילים בני אדם לזרוע, וסגי ליה בשני מעשרות, במעשר ראשון ומעשר שני. אבל דבר של איסור, אין רגילין בני אדם לזרוע; והואיל ואיהו קא זרע באיסורא, שזרעה בלא תרומה ומעשר, קנסינן ליה השתא שמעשר אותו עישור שהיה לו ליתן אשתקד, שלא ישתכר בכך:
Rashi on Nedarim 59b:3:2.english: Permitted [produce] people sow - Something that is tithed, people are accustomed to sow, and two tithes suffice for it — first tithe and second tithe. However, something that is forbidden, people are not accustomed to sow; and since he sowed [it] in a forbidden manner, for he sowed it without [separating] terumah and tithe, we penalize him now so that he tithes that [same] tithe that he had to give last year, so that he will not profit from this.

Tosafot on Nedarim 59b:1:1.hebrew: אם היו עלין [שלהן] שחורין אסורין - אף מה שגדלו בששית, אלמא היתר דידהו פקע:
Tosafot on Nedarim 59b:1:1.english: If [their] leaves were black, they are forbidden - Even what grew in the sixth [year is forbidden]; thus, their permitted [status] has expired.

Tosafot on Nedarim 59b:1:2.english: Rav Ḥisda said to him: Do you maintain [that] it teaches "they are forbidden" regarding the primary [onion]? It teaches [this] regarding the additional [growth] - but regarding the primary [onion], it is permitted if it is distinguishable from the [new] growth:

Tosafot on Nedarim 59b:1:3.hebrew: א"ה - דלת"ק אין איסור אלא בגידולין לבד, מאי אתא למימר דתני ר"ג: "הגדל בחיוב חייב, הגדל בפטור פטור"? רבן גמליאל [קאמר] אפי' עליהן שרי, ואינם אסורין אלא הגדל בחיוב — כלומר באיסור שביעית — אבל הגדל בפטור, כלומר בהיתר קודם שביעית. ונהי דאין העיקר ניכר וכולו אסור, מכל מקום נפקא מינה במה שהעיקר מותר, שאינו צריך ששים רק מן הגידולין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 59b:1:3.english: "If so" - Since according to the first tanna there is no prohibition except on the [new] growth alone, what is [he] coming to say, as Rabban Gamliel teaches: "That which grew during [a period of] liability is liable; that which grew during [a period of] exemption is exempt"? Rabban Gamliel [is saying that] even their leaves are permitted, and nothing is forbidden except that which grew during [a period of] liability — that is, under the prohibition of the Sabbatical Year — whereas that which grew during [a period of] exemption, that is, in a state of permissibility before the Sabbatical Year, [is permitted]. And although the primary [onion] is not distinguishable and the entire [onion] is forbidden, nevertheless there is a practical difference in that the primary [onion] is permitted, for one does not need sixty [times the entire onion to nullify it], only [sixty times] the [new] growth.

Tosafot on Nedarim 59b:1:4.hebrew: ת״ק נמי הכי קאמר - בתמיה, דלדידך דאמרת דלת״ק אינו אוסר אלא הגידולין. ה״ג: "כולה מתניתין ר״ג [קתני לה] (דלת״ק אינו אסור אלא גידולין), ועד כאן לא שמיע ליה לר״ג דלא טרח, אבל טרח — בטל ברוב". כך השיב לו רבה, דסבירא ליה דהתר פקע. וקאמר דר״ג נמי, דאמר "גדלו בפטור — פטור", מודה הכא בליטרא בצל שתיקנה וזרעה שהיתר שבו פקע; דהתם במילתי' דר״ג לא טרח בגידולין, ומאיליהם הם באים — הלכך לא חשיבי לבטל העיקר, אבל בבצל דטרח בגידולין והחשיבם — מבטלין את העיקר. ואמר הר״ם דהאי טעמא דטרח ולא טרח היינו כדאמר במנחות פרק רבי ישמעאל (מנחות דף ע -) גבי הך דבצל שתיקנה: דהכא — דטרח בנטיעתו, אבל התם בגידולין דשביעית — לאו היינו נטיעתו, כלו' אין הנטיעה באיסור, שבערב שביעית נטועי' ובאים משביעית, אבל הכא תחלת נטיעתה [באה בשביעית] — לכך מבטלין גידולין לעיקר. ודבר זה מגומגם, דליתא להך מילתא דר״ג גבי הך ברייתא "ואם היו שחורים עליהן":
Tosafot on Nedarim 59b:1:4.english: The first tanna also says this - [This is asked] as a rhetorical question, for according to you, who say that according to the first tanna only the growths are forbidden. This is how we read [the text]: "Rabban Gamliel [taught] the entire mishna (according to the first tanna, only the growths are forbidden), and you have only heard Rabban Gamliel [say this] where he did not exert himself, but where he exerted himself, it is nullified by the majority." Thus Rabbah answered him, as he holds that the permitted [part] ceases [to exist]. And he says that Rabban Gamliel as well, who said, "That which grew during [a period of] exemption is exempt," concedes here regarding a litra of onion that one tithed and sowed, that the permitted [part] in it ceases [to exist]. For there, in Rabban Gamliel's statement, he did not exert himself over the growths, and they come on their own; therefore, they are not significant [enough] to nullify the primary [part]. However, regarding the onion, where he exerted himself over the growths and made them significant, they nullify the primary [part]. And the R"M said that this reason of "exerted himself" versus "did not exert himself" is as it says in Menachot, in the chapter Rabbi Yishmael (Menachot 70a), regarding this [case] of the onion that one tithed: that here, he exerted himself in its planting, whereas there, regarding the growths of the Sabbatical year, that is not its planting — meaning, the planting is not [done] in [a state of] prohibition, for they were planted on the eve of the Sabbatical year and [only] come [up] during the Sabbatical year; whereas here, the beginning of its planting [came during the Sabbatical year], therefore the growths nullify the primary [part]. And this matter is garbled, for this statement of Rabban Gamliel does not appear in connection with this baraita, "And if their leaves were black":

Tosafot on Nedarim 59b:3:1.hebrew: והרי ליטרא מעשר טבל - פי' לעיל. אלמא אף על גב דלא קא טרח, לא קמבטלי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 59b:3:1.english: And isn't there [the case of] a litra of untithed tithe - [This was] explained above. Thus, even though he does not exert himself, they do not nullify [it].

Tosafot on Nedarim 59b:3:2.hebrew: שאני התם - בהך דקאמר דמתעשר לפי כולה, דאמר קרא "עשר תעשר את תבואת זרעך", אלמא תבואה זרועה בעי לעשורי כל המעשרות. והך נמי שתיקנה הוי סתם זריעה, דהיתירא זרעי, אבל איסור לא זרעי — שאין דרך לזרוע מעשר עצמו כשאינו מתוקן לתרומת מעשר, ומינה לא איירי קרא; הלכך לא בטל, ולא בעי לעשורי כבתחלה כיון דטרח בטלה. אבל בהך ליטרא שתיקנה, דהיינו כדרך שבני אדם מוציאין לזריעה, יש לנו להעמיד בזה קרא ד"עשר תעשר", שצריך לחזור ולעשר כבתחלה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 59b:3:2.english: It is different there - Regarding that which [the baraita] says that it is tithed according to all of it, for the verse states: "You shall tithe all the produce of your seed," thus, sown produce must have all the tithes separated [from it]. And this [litra] as well, once one has rectified it, is [considered] ordinary sowing, for permitted [produce] people sow, whereas forbidden [produce] they do not sow — for it is not customary to sow tithe itself when it is not rectified with respect to terumat ma'aser, and of it the verse does not speak; therefore, it is not nullified, and [one] does not need to tithe [it] as at first, since he exerted himself [and] it is nullified. However, regarding this litra that he rectified, which is in the manner that people take out [seed] for sowing, we must apply to this the verse "You shall tithe," [teaching] that one must go back and tithe [it] as at first.

Tosafot on Nedarim 59b:4:1.english: Returning to the matter itself: Rabbi Chanina Tirta'a said, "An onion of terumah, etc., is permitted" - For it becomes non-sacred [produce] and is permitted to non-priests.
